title: A fresh worktree reuses the clone's pack index for unchanged content
goal: A fresh git worktree of a clone, at content the clone already indexed, finds that pack index instead of rebuilding it: the index key no longer depends on the checkout's path or the files' mtimes, and the worktrees of one clone share the index directory, so the first rag.py pack in a new worktree takes under 5 s on the Windows host where it took 14 s; an edit of any indexed file still gives a new index, a server holding an index open never has it pruned by another worktree, and tests that test index building keep their own index directory.

run: import subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,time,os,shutil;q=[sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','pack','kerberos delegation'];s.run(q,capture_output=True,check=True);d=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'wt');s.run(['git','worktree','add','-q','--detach',d],check=True);t=time.time();r=s.run([sys.executable,os.path.join(d,'_tools','rag.py'),'pack','kerberos delegation'],cwd=d,capture_output=True);e=time.time()-t;shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True);s.run(['git','worktree','prune']);print('fresh worktree first pack',round(e,2),'s exit',r.returncode);sys.exit(r.returncode or int(e>5))

links: kb/public/python/pytest-xdist.md (session fixture once per worker, FileLock pattern)
notes: Deferred, outside any sprint: kbfacts.fingerprint hashes each file's mtime_ns and the absolute root paths, so a clone at another path never matches the seed's index file and a copied index is never read. It needs a fingerprint independent of the clone's path and mtimes (_tools/kbfacts.py, outside these touches) and a Windows measurement first: on the Mac a fresh clone's first rag.py pack costs about 3 s cold against 0.05 s warm, about 10% of the scenario files' time; the Windows premise (check.py 14.5 s cold, 25-35% of worker time) is file-cache and Defender cost. kbfacts.store() prunes other indexes of its root in the same directory, so a shared KB_INDEX directory across scenarios could delete a file another test holds open on Windows; a per-clone copy avoids that. Its checks name perfcheck.py (ST-c35i7vjx). Its full tests.py and perfcheck ids checks pass before the work by design: they guard that the speed-up loses no test; -k seed_index and the time bound are what the work must make pass. Housekeeping 2026-10-06: the -k seed_index selector and 'perfcheck time tests --max 900' went with the old suite; the time bound is now perfcheck time --max-seconds 60, the Windows ceiling of _tools/tests_ceiling.json, and the worker proves the reuse by a tool run on a planted scenario clone, not by a new test. 2026-10-07: the time bound follows the win32 ceiling raised to 150 s (D-776rvpx2, gate ceiling of ST-pg5jyebo). 2026-10-07 Windows premise: a fresh clone's first pack takes 14.0 s cold vs 0.17 s warm; a full tests.py logging each store() build showed no scenario clone builds an index. Reshaped 2026-10-07 by the operator after the premise measurement: scenario clones build no index, but a fresh worktree's first pack costs 14 s cold on the Windows host (0.17 s warm), since kbfacts.fingerprint hashes mtimes and absolute root paths and index_path puts the index in each checkout's _cache/. The rebuild after a kb or kbfacts.py edit is a separate story.
